fixes.explanation: Good guess, baker, because the altar does come up earlier, back in verses 5 to 7. But when Moses and the Levitical priests speak to all Israel, the first thing they say is, “Be silent, O Israel, and listen!” (Deuteronomy 27:9). The altar instructions were already given before that. Here the command is to hush up and hear.

Yes, baker! Look at the verb in that curse. It isn't about pushing him or tripping him. The curse lands on the man who “…lets a blind man wander in the road.” (Deuteronomy 27:18). So letting it happen is what gets named. It's like seeing a friend about to send a message to the wrong group chat and just letting it go through.

Yes, baker. Justice is the word, and the verb matters just as much: “withholds.” The curse is on the one who holds justice back from the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow (Deuteronomy 27:19). Nothing here says he took anything. He kept it from them. And Moses says that after each curse in this list, all the people are to say, “Amen!”

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.

The passage records a command to be silent and listen, not the crowd becoming quiet and listening. It has also already instructed the people to cross the Jordan and build an altar, so saying nobody has been told to take a step yet is misleading.
The verse does not say the person is standing there, doing nothing at all, or rule out shoving or tripping. It says the cursed person lets a blind man wander in the road.
Moses instructs the people to say Amen after each curse; the passage does not say they actually answer at this point.
